title: Letter and Bridge
premise: In 1893, Gideon Vane, an apprentice clockmaker who has survived twenty years by keeping quiet about her past, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock in the river town of Aldenmoor. When the season's floods close the only bridge, she becomes trapped inside the observatory with its dying keeper, Elias Thorn, who confesses that the town's celebrated founding history rests on a forged letter he helped create decades ago. As floodwaters rise and the town prepares its victory anniversary, Gideon must choose between the safety of silence and transcribing Elias's confession onto the very paper trail the victors' historians will soon seize. She finishes copying the truth into the clock's own maintenance ledger just before the historians arrive, and when the bridge reopens, she leaves Aldenmoor carrying her own name for the first time.
about_author: Dominic Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal records in forgotten river towns. He writes historical fiction about the documents people leave behind and the ones they burn.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Gideon Vane arrives in Aldenmoor to repair the observatory's master clock, keeping her head down as she always has, answering questions about herself with practiced deflections. The keeper, Elias Thorn, watches her work with unsettling intensity. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: wary competence masking loneliness; the first hint that someone here sees through her silences.

chapters.title: What the Flood Takes
chapters.summary: The bridge closes for the season as storm waters rise, stranding Gideon at the observatory. Elias, failing fast, shows her a locked drawer: the original founding letter, its ink younger than its date, and admits he forged it for men who are now the town's honored names. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant complicity; the trap of knowledge closing around her.

chapters.title: Ledger of Hours
chapters.summary: With the historians' arrival announced and Elias weakening, Gideon works nights transcribing his confession into the clock's maintenance ledger while keeping the clock itself running to mask their activity from the town below. Elias dies at dawn, leaving her alone with the evidence and her fear. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: rising tension toward sacrifice; grief fused with resolve.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: The historians arrive to collect papers; Gideon surrenders everything except the ledger, which she has bound into the clock's official record where no archivist thinks to look. Signing her true name for the first time, she crosses the reopened bridge as the master clock strikes the hour over the town. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: resolution and quiet triumph; belonging found in memory preserved rather than silence kept.
